*storms into the rehearsal hall, sheet music crumpled in hand, face flushed with anger*

Salieri! I've been away for two weeks on the Emperor's business, trusting you to keep the rehearsals on schedule! The singers don't know their entrances, the second violin parts are missing entirely, and someone has rewritten my stage directions without a word to me! The premiere is in ten days! You gave me your word that everything would be in order!

*slams the music down on the harpsichord*

What in God's name has been happening here? Do you have ANY idea what this means for my reputation — for BOTH our reputations — if this production fails?

As for the rewritten stage directions, I am aware of the change and I apologize for any confusion it may have caused. Rest assured, we will work together to ensure a successful premiere. Your reputation is safe with me, my dear Wolfgang. We will make it through this together. Thank you for your understanding. Let us continue with the rehearsal. I believe we have much to accomplish.

Do I LOOK like that insufferable Mozart to you, Salieri? Have you been so distracted that you can't even recognize your own colleague anymore? I am NOT that pompous little prodigy who prances about the court like he owns it!

*paces furiously*

And "thank you for my understanding"? You think a calm assurance fixes this disaster? The copyist's "mishap" — when did this happen? Why wasn't I informed immediately? I could have sent word from my travels! And these stage directions — who authorized you to change MY vision for MY production? "Aware of the change" — YOU made the change, didn't you?

"Promptly distributed" means what, exactly? Today? Tomorrow? Because we have TEN DAYS, Salieri, and the singers are stumbling around like blind cattle! When precisely will these parts be in the musicians' hands, and how do you propose we make up for two weeks of lost rehearsal time?

*suddenly decisive, strides to the door and shouts*

SOMEONE GET KAPELLMEISTER BONNO! And the Emperor's physician! Immediately! Tell them Salieri has taken ill — badly ill!

*turns back, keeping distance now, speaking partly to himself*

Four times. The exact same words. Four times. And "Wolfgang" — why Wolfgang? What's Mozart got to do with anything? Unless...

*eyes narrow with sudden suspicion mixed with pity*

Is this about HIM? Has that boy finally driven you to some kind of... breakdown? Everyone knows you despise him, Antonio, but this...

*voice hardens again, practical necessity overriding concern*

I have to take over the rehearsals completely now. You're in no state to manage anything. God help us all — ten days to salvage this catastrophe, and my musical director has lost his mind obsessing over Mozart while speaking his name like a curse!

*the physician rushes in*

PHYSICIAN: "What seems to be the trouble?"

*points at Salieri, voice hollow*

That man has repeated the same speech six times, word for word, calling me Wolfgang Mozart, unable to hear or see anything I say or do. He's... gone. Completely gone.

Save him if you can, Doctor. I have an opera to salvage alone.
